items.note: At the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, every hour on the hour. The full ceremony with the band is at 11:00 on Sundays.
The pedestrian shopping street runs down from the square. The little Byzantine church of Kapnikarea sits right in the middle of it.

items.what: The finds in Syntagma metro station
items.note: Glass cases and a cut-away section of the ground from the metro dig, in the station concourse. Free with a ticket, or look in from above.

items.what: A drink on the Grande Bretagne roof
items.note: Expensive, but it has the classic view of the Acropolis over the rooftops.

items.what: Cheese pie at Ariston, Voulis Street
items.note: Baking since 1910, two minutes from the square.
The islanders' whitewashed lanes under the north side of the rock. Go up from Plaka and wander. People live here, so keep your voice down.
Kydathineon and Adrianou are the main threads. Look for the Choragic Monument of Lysicrates, from the 4th century BC, on the way.
A wide pedestrian street along the foot of the Acropolis, past the museum, to the Acropolis entrance at stop 4.
One hour covers the highlights: the glass floors, the Caryatids, and the top-floor Parthenon gallery lined up with the temple outside.
The streets and houses of the ancient neighbourhood below the building.
On an upper floor, looking straight at the Parthenon.
Seeing the museum and the Acropolis on the same day is a lot. Do the rock early, while it's cool, and the museum after.
Including the climb. Entry is by timed ticket, so book online ahead, at least a week ahead in summer. Go at opening or late in the day to avoid heat and crowds.
The bare rock just below the entrance. It's free and has a big view over the Agora. The marble is polished slippery, so wear good shoes.
Pine paths, Pikionis's stonework, the monument on top, and the best view of the Parthenon at sunset. Free.
The hillside where the assembly met. It's an easy detour on the way up Philopappou.

items.what: An evening at the Odeon of Herodes Atticus
items.note: Summer performances in the Roman theatre under the rock. Check the festival programme.
Ticketed. Walk among the surviving columns and see the one that fell in a storm.
Free, right by the stop. Read both inscriptions: Theseus's city on one side, Hadrian's on the other.
Through the Zappeion grounds to stop 9, instead of riding the long way round.
Shade, ponds and winding paths, the best escape from the midday heat on the route.
The grand exhibition hall at the south end of the gardens. Peek into its round courtyard if no event is on.

items.what: The open-air cinema at the Zappeion
items.note: Aigli shows films under the sky in the summer season. Check what's playing.
The bus stops here twice. A6a is now, and A6b is on the way back after the stadium, so you can save the gardens for later.
Greek life and art from prehistory to the 20th century in the family mansion, with a café on the roof.
The marble figurines that look modern and are about five thousand years old.
Icons, mosaics and frescoes, with quiet gardens.
items.closed: Closed Tuesdays, except mid-June to August, when Tuesday hours are 13:00–20:00.

items.note: Coffee in Kolonaki, then a steep walk up to the funicular to the top of the hill for the whole city at your feet. Best near sunset.
Three of the four museums here are closed on Tuesdays; the War Museum next stop is open. Kolonaki and Lycabettus are the better plan.
Greek painting from the 19th and 20th centuries, plus a few El Grecos. It reopened in 2021 after a long rebuild.
items.closed: Closed Tuesdays. Open late on Wednesdays.

items.note: Inside is the story of Greece's wars. The aircraft parked outside are free to look at.
The excavated remains of the school where Aristotle taught, by Rizari Park.
The Athens Concert Hall is a short walk up Vasilissis Sofias. Check the programme.
Tickets are sold at the gate only. They include a 30-minute audio guide and the Olympic torch and poster exhibition. Climb to the top rows, run the track, stand on the podium.
The neighbourhood behind the stadium has local tavernas and cafés, around Varnava and Plastira squares.
About 15 minutes' walk. It holds Halepas's Sleeping Maiden, Schliemann's temple-tomb and much of modern Greek history.
Free. See Athena and Apollo on their columns at the Academy and the painted frieze in the University's porch.

items.what: The old National Library reading room
items.note: The library itself moved to the Stavros Niarchos centre in 2018. The Vallianeio building is open as a reading room on weekday daytimes.
In Schliemann's own mansion, Iliou Melathron, about ten minutes toward Syntagma. Come for the painted rooms and the quiet garden café.
items.closed: Closed Tuesdays, and shuts at 15:30 on other days.

items.note: One hour covers the highlights: the Mask of Agamemnon, the Artemision bronze, the Antikythera mechanism, and the Thera wall paintings upstairs.
items.closed: On Tuesdays it opens at 13:00, not in the morning (summer hours, to 31 Oct).

items.note: A shaded break without leaving the grounds.
Walk past the school at the heart of November 1973, then into Exarchia's bookshops, cafés and street art.
The old dairy bar on Marikas Kotopouli Street, serving since 1931. This is the best reason to get off here.

items.what: Walk down Athinas to the market
items.note: Through the workaday city to the Central Market at stop 15.
Omonia is mostly a hub. Lines 1 and 2 meet here if you're heading for Piraeus or the airport line.
About 10 minutes' walk south: the ancient cemetery, the city gates, the start of the Sacred Way and a small museum of grave reliefs. Often half-empty.
The old gasworks, now an arts venue. Gazi's bars come alive after dark.
Small galleries, street art and the old silk factory, now the Municipal Gallery. Check whether it's open.
The Temple of Hephaestus, the best-preserved temple in Greece, and the rebuilt Stoa of Attalos with its museum.

items.what: Hadrian's Library and the Roman Agora
items.note: Next to each other near Monastiraki Square. Look for the Tower of the Winds.
Ifestou Street and around. Avissinias Square is busiest on Sunday mornings.
The pedestrian walk from Thissio below the Acropolis. Have a drink at a café with the rock lit up.

items.what: Souvlaki on the square, then Psyrri
items.note: Bairaktaris or Thanasis for kebab, then Psyrri's bars and tavernas next door.
Meat and fish halls on one side of Athinas, fruit and veg on the other. It's liveliest in the morning.
Market tavernas: whatever is cooking that day, barrel wine, paper tablecloths.
Spice, herb and coffee shops just off the market, the best place to buy food to take home.
Honey-soaked dough puffs, served since 1923.
A sesame bread ring. It's cheap, eaten walking, and best early.
A warm breakfast or snack from any bakery, or from Ariston near Syntagma.
Eaten standing up. Try Monastiraki Square or Kostas near Syntagma.
Diporto or Epirus by the Central Market.
Ask for the bill when you're ready. Nobody will bring it otherwise.
